title: Editing or Deleting an On-Premises File Server

blocks.text: You can modify or delete an on-premises file server as required.
To edit an on-premises file server:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Service Registration.
On the Service Registration page, select the On-Premises File Servers tab.
Do one of the following:
Click the Actions icon (), and select Edit for the required file server.
See image.
Click the name of the file server to open the On-Premises File Server details drawer, then click Actions, and select Edit.
See image.
The Edit On-Premises File Server confirmation window appears.
In the Edit On-Premises File Server confirmation window, click Proceed to continue.
See image.
In the Edit On-Premises File Server drawer, update the following sections as required:
File Server Information:
Version (only for NFS protocol): Select the NFS version to use.
Connection Attributes:
File Server IP / Hostname: Update the IP address or hostname of the file server.
For an NFS protocol and NetApp file server type, enter the hostname only.
Domain Name: Update the domain name associated with the file server.
Port: Update the port used for communication protocol.
Default Port: SMB uses 445 and NFS uses 2049.
Custom Port: Enter a valid port number based on your configuration requirements.
Authentication:
The authentication fields available depend on the Protocol and File Server Type selected.
Secret Provider Type: This field is automatically populated with the provider used to manage authentication secrets, typically set to Zscaler DSPM.
Authentication Type: Select the authentication method used to access file shares:
Kerberos: Uses Kerberos-based authentication to access file shares.
AUTH_SYS: Uses system-level User Identifier (UID) or Group Identifier (GID) credentials for authentication.
NTLMv2: Uses NT LAN Manager (NTLM) authentication to access file shares.
Username: Enter the username used to authenticate access to the file server.
Password: Enter the password associated with the username.
Group IDs: Enter one or more GIDs that have access to the file share, separated by commas.
The following table lists the availability of each field based on the selected protocol and file server type:

table: Available only when NetApp is selected as the file server type.
Available for NFS or SMB protocol with NetApp file server type.
Available for NFS protocol with NetApp file server type only.
Available for SMB protocol with NetApp file server type only.
Available for Windows or Linux file server types, or when Kerberos or NTLMv2 is selected for NetApp.
Available for Windows or Linux file server types, or when Kerberos or NTLMv2 is selected for NetApp.
Available only when AUTH_SYS is selected as the Authentication Type.

blocks.item: LDAP Server: (available only when SMB is selected as the protocol)
Server (Optional): Select the registered Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) server for the on-premises file server.
See image.
Click Save.

blocks.text: The on-premises file server is updated.
Changes made to the on-premises file server configuration take effect only at the next scheduled scan.
To delete an on-premises file server:

blocks.item: Go to Data Security > DSPM > Service Registration.
On the Service Registration page, select the On-Premises File Servers tab.
Do one of the following:
Click the Actions icon (), and select Delete for the required file server.
See image.
Click the name of the file server to open the On-Premises File Server details drawer, then click Actions, and select Delete.
See image.
The Delete On-Premises File Server confirmation window appears.
In the Delete On-Premises File Server confirmation window, read the message, and then enter CONFIRM in the text box.
See image.
Click Delete Server.

blocks.text: The on-premises file server is deleted from the Zscaler Admin Console.
